hints: Think about what you know from the lab, limestone in water versus clear limewater solution.
Remember that $\text{CaCO}_3$ is essentially insoluble, while $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is sparingly soluble enough to make limewater.
Now recall the lime cycle starting from limestone, thermal decomposition to quicklime then slaking with water to make slaked lime.
walkthrough:
**Compare the solubilities**

Think side by side. Calcium carbonate, limestone, chalk and marble, does not dissolve in water.

Calcium hydroxide is sparingly soluble, about 1 g per dm3, and its aqueous solution is limewater, $\text{Ca(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}$.

**Decide the first statement**

Since limewater exists but there is no equivalent carbonate solution, calcium hydroxide is more soluble.

So the claim: $$\text{calcium carbonate is more soluble than calcium hydroxide}$$ is false. Answer is no.

**Check the manufacture route**

Limestone is the cheap starting material for the lime cycle. Heat it strongly, then add water:
$$\text{CaCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$\text{CaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2$$
So calcium hydroxide can indeed be made from calcium carbonate. Answer is yes, giving no then yes.

options.A: First part no is correct because $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is more soluble than $\text{CaCO}_3$, but second part no is wrong. The thermal decomposition of $\text{CaCO}_3$ to $\text{CaO}$ followed by $\text{CaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is the standard industrial route.
options.B: Exactly right. $\text{CaCO}_3$ is virtually insoluble while $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is sparingly soluble (limewater), so the first statement is no. And $\text{CaCO}_3$ is heated to $\text{CaO}$ then slaked to $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$, so the second statement is yes.
options.C: Both parts are reversed. $\text{CaCO}_3$ is less soluble, not more soluble, than $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$, and $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ certainly can be made from $\text{CaCO}_3$. This choice confuses which solid forms limewater.
options.D: Second part yes is correct for the lime cycle, but first part yes is wrong. Students sometimes think all carbonates dissolve or forget that limewater proves $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ has the higher solubility.
